parts.visual:
A founder realizes their company will run out of money in 30 days. Option A: They stop answering investor emails, fire everyone over Zoom without warning, and disappear to Mexico. Option B: They call a board meeting, explain exactly why the market shifted, help their employees find new jobs, and return the remaining $50,000 to the investors.

The Autopsy:
1. 90% Fail: Failure in Silicon Valley is not a bug; it is the core feature of the ecosystem. VCs expect 9 out of 10 companies to die.
2. The Graceful Exit: How a founder acts during the death of their company determines their entire future career. If you fail with honor, integrity, and transparency, the exact same VCs will fund your next company.
parts.audio: Silicon Valley does not punish failure. Silicon Valley severely punishes cowardice, lying, and hiding from your investors when the ship is sinking. If you are going to crash the airplane, look the passengers in the eye while you do it.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a 'Post-Mortem' document?
options: Intellectual Honesty. It is a highly detailed, brutally honest document the founder writes after bankruptcy, explaining exactly what hypotheses were wrong, what mistakes were made, and what the industry can learn from the death of the startup.
questions.correct_answer: Intellectual Honesty. It is a highly detailed, brutally honest document the founder writes after bankruptcy, explaining exactly what hypotheses were wrong, what mistakes were made, and what the industry can learn from the death of the startup.
questions.explanation: Failure without learning is just a waste of money.

questions.question: Listen to the VC explaining why they funded a founder who had previously lost them $2 Million.
questions.tts_text: When his last company failed, he didn't hide. He called me every week to give me bad news. He spent his last weeks helping his engineers get hired at Google. He showed elite character under pressure. I will back him forever.
options: Because the VC likes losing money.

Character Validation. Startups are chaos. A VC cannot truly know a founder's character when everything is going perfectly. A massive failure is the ultimate stress-test of a founder's integrity and leadership. If they pass the test, they are heavily rewarded.
Because the founder bought them dinner.
questions.correct_answer: Character Validation. Startups are chaos. A VC cannot truly know a founder's character when everything is going perfectly. A massive failure is the ultimate stress-test of a founder's integrity and leadership. If they pass the test, they are heavily rewarded.
questions.explanation: You earn trust in the dark, not the light.

questions.question: What is the worst possible legal mistake a founder can make when the company is running out of cash?
options: Failing to pay payroll taxes. If a startup goes bankrupt, the corporate shield usually protects the founder's personal money. But if the founder stops paying government payroll taxes to try and save the company, the government can pierce the shield and seize the founder's personal house.
questions.correct_answer: Failing to pay payroll taxes. If a startup goes bankrupt, the corporate shield usually protects the founder's personal money. But if the founder stops paying government payroll taxes to try and save the company, the government can pierce the shield and seize the founder's personal house.
questions.explanation: Never mess with the IRS to buy one more week of runway.

questions.question: What does 'Fiduciary Duty' mean in the final days of a startup?
options: The legal obligation of the CEO to act in the best financial interest of the shareholders, NOT themselves. If the company is dying, the CEO must sell off the laptops, patents, and servers to return whatever tiny amount of cash is left to the investors.
The duty to lie to the press.
questions.correct_answer: The legal obligation of the CEO to act in the best financial interest of the shareholders, NOT themselves. If the company is dying, the CEO must sell off the laptops, patents, and servers to return whatever tiny amount of cash is left to the investors.
questions.explanation: The captain goes down with the ship, but must save the cargo.

questions.explanation: How you fail dictates if you are allowed to try again.
